units.headline: Record lookup failures no longer fail loadMetadata/Track
units.summary: For KindRecord items, loadMetadata now ignores any error from getRecord and returns metadata holding only the parsed record key, so Track always succeeds. Before, Track returned the error. Now the item is stored with no owner, and nothing refreshes that later.
focus: Transient errors (timeouts, connect failures) are now swallowed the same way as permanent FORBIDDEN replies
Track stores the metadata once, so an item tracked during an outage never gets its owner
Callers of Track that relied on the error to retry or to reject the item

issues.title: Transient lookup errors permanently drop owner for tracked item
issues.detail: Every getRecord error is discarded, including timeouts and connection failures, not just permanent error replies. Track then stores metadata with an empty Owner, and nothing triggers a later refresh.
issues.failure_scenario: The inventory server is briefly unreachable, so connect fails or the context deadline hits during Track. Before this PR Track returned an error and the caller could retry. Now the item is tracked with no owner and stays that way for as long as it is tracked.

units.reason: Changes error propagation: Track no longer fails on lookup errors, which changes the stored owner data.

units.headline: New tests for client error/success caching and loadMetadata fallback
units.summary: New tests cover per-key error caching with TTL expiry, success caching, isErrorReply with wrapped errors, and the loadMetadata fallback. They inject fakes through the client's get/now fields. The fake returns ReplyError unwrapped, which matches what fetchFromServer passes through from conn.Get. These are test-only additions.
units.reason: New test file only; it cannot affect production behavior.
